name: as-morphology-comparison
title: Three Morphologies' Sensing
question: How do the three morphologies differ in what they can sense, and which is the agent analyzed here?
claim: The three morphologies differ in chemosensor placement and whether they have internal nutrient sensors; the evolved, analyzed agent is morphology M2 (one front stalk + nutrient sensors).

expected_behavior.name: morphology-sensing-characterized
expected_behavior.rationale: M1 = two side stalks (±90 deg) + nutrient sensors (6 sensors); M2 = one front stalk + nutrient sensors (4 sensors); M3 = two stalks, NO nutrient sensors (4 sensors). Verified by the body's sensor_layout.

findings.summary: M2 (one front stalk + nutrient sensors) is the evolved, switching agent; M1/M3 shown structurally.
findings.detail: figures/morphologies.png diagrams the three sensor layouts. M3 lacks internal nutrient sensors, so it would have to internalize nutrient state to switch — evolving M1/M3 is a documented extension.

config.caption: The three morphologies' sensor layouts (Agmon & Beer Fig. 2): chemosensor stalks (red=A, green=B) + nutrient sensors.

derived.insight: M2 (one front stalk + nutrient sensors) is the evolved, switching agent; M1/M3 shown structurally.
